metadata.case_name: LAW MUK YAU v. SO CHEUK PO T/A PO KEE LOGISTICS

injuries.description: Avulsion fracture of the triquetrum of the left wrist
source: Further X-ray of left wrist showed avulsion fracture of the triquetrum.
His diagnosis was avulsion fracture of the triquetrum.

manifestations.description: Residual pain of left wrist and hand
Decrease of range of movement of left wrist
Weakness of left hand and wrist
Reduced work efficiency and competitiveness due to left wrist limitations

treatments_received.treatment: Attendance at Accident & Emergency Department, Queen Elizabeth Hospital (QEH)
source: After the injuries, the Plaintiff continued to work for the rest of the morning. However, due to increased left wrist and hand pain, he attended the Accident & Emergency Department of Queen Elizabeth Hospital (“QEH”) the following day.
He re-attended QEH on 9th May, 2010, 12th May, 2010 and 26th May, 2010 for persistent pain.

treatments_received.treatment: Follow-up clinic attendances at QEH A&E follow-up clinic (4 attendances)
source: Apart from receiving treatment from the follow-up clinic, the Plaintiff was referred to occupational therapy for management of wrist pain on 26th May 2010.
Follow-up Clinic of A & E Dept. of the QEH, 4 attendances $240.00
A wrist resting splint was provided on the same day.
the Plaintiff was referred to occupational therapy for management of wrist pain on 26th May 2010.

treatments_received.treatment: Physiotherapy, 14 sessions from 2nd July, 2010 to 1st September, 2010
source: He also received a total of 14 sessions of physiotherapy in QEH from 2nd July, 2010 to 1st September, 2010.

losses.description: Residual pain, decreased range of movement, weakness and cramp in the left wrist and hand
Unable to return to work as a master baker; now working as a baking assistant with reduced tasks and earning approximately $2,000 less per month
